title: Lower Shell Skin Panel at the Fwd Cargo Door Corner — External Patch Repair

issue.reason: Issue C. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Permanent external patch repair for crack and corrosion damage in the lower shell skin panel beside the forward cargo door aperture, with an attached fatigue life limit and a repeat surface inspection.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the static strength and the residual fatigue capability of the lower shell skin panel next to the forward cargo door aperture after the removal of crack or corrosion damage.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the extent of the damage by detailed visual inspection followed by an eddy current inspection of the surrounding area to a radius of at least 150 mm. Damage inside the allowable limits below may be blended out and left unrepaired. Damage that crosses a fastener row, that reaches the aperture radius, or that lies within 40 mm of an existing repair is outside the scope of this repair and needs an engineering assessment. Record the damage position relative to the nearest frame station and stringer before any material is removed, because the patch layout is set from it and the reference is lost once routing starts.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the damaged material by routing to a smooth oval with a minimum corner radius of 12 mm and blend the edges. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the routed edge. Cut the external patch from 1.6 mm titanium sheet to the layout of the repair drawing and drill the fastener pattern using the patch as a template. Deburr every hole and apply the surface protection of the standard practice to all new surfaces. Install the patch wet with sealant, using solid countersunk rivets AES645587-2A on the two outer rows at the pitch and edge distance given on the drawing. Where the patch footprint crosses the lower fitting D5321120273903, add the local packer shown on sheet 2. Where the stiffener CIN650686-39 lies under the patch, transfer the fastener pattern into it rather than fitting a blind fastener. Restore the external finish to aerodynamic smoothness class B and re-seal the panel edge.
sections.inspection_requirements: This repair is life limited to 14 000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment. Do a repeat eddy current inspection of the patch perimeter and of the routed edge every 4 000 flight cycles. Any new indication inside the repair boundary makes the repair invalid and needs a new engineering assessment. Report the repair to Aeralis with the damage map so that it is recorded against the aircraft, because the area is under fleet-wide fatigue surveillance.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 20 mm in length that do not cross a fastener row, are not closer than 15 mm to a fastener centre, and are not closer than 40 mm to the door aperture radius. One crack per skin bay.

repair_drawings.title: External patch, fwd cargo door lower corner skin panel

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two rows of 32 rivets, 22 mm pitch, 16 mm edge distance, staggered
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Life limited to 14 000 flight cycles; repeat eddy current inspection of the patch perimeter every 4 000 flight cycles.
